# Decoding Fuel Range: From Tank Capacity to Cost Per Mile

Determining how far a vehicle can travel on a full tank isn't just about reading the dashboard; it's a calculation that bridges mechanical specifications, current market rates, and real-world driving dynamics. Whether you are looking at an Audi TT or a Lexus IS 200, the methodology remains consistent across almost any internal combustion engine vehicle. The process involves isolating three distinct variables: tank capacity, fuel economy, and local pricing.

### Isolating Tank Capacity

The first step is establishing the raw volume of the fuel system. Manufacturers typically publish this figure in liters or gallons in the owner's manual or technical specification sheet. However, there is a critical distinction often overlooked: the difference between *total capacity* and *usable capacity*. The total capacity represents the physical volume of the tank, whereas usable capacity accounts for the space required to prevent fuel starvation during sharp maneuvers or steep inclines. For precise calculations, you should rely on the usable figure if it is explicitly listed; otherwise, assume the published total capacity is the baseline.

If you need to verify this data without consulting documentation, you can perform a physical audit. Fill the tank until the pump automatically clicks off, then fill it again once or twice more while keeping track of every liter added. This "fill-to-fill" method captures the actual usable volume, accounting for the reserve fuel that sits at the bottom of the tank to protect the pump and ensure delivery under load.

### Calculating Cost Per Mile

Once you have the volume (let's call it $V$ in liters) and your vehicle's average fuel consumption ($MPG$ or L/100km), you can determine how far a full tank takes you. It is vital to distinguish between the *ideal* range calculated from official MPG figures and the *real-world* range, which will likely be lower due to traffic, terrain, and driving style.

To find the cost of covering that distance, you must apply the current price per unit of fuel. In the UK, fuel prices fluctuate frequently, so relying on a static historical average can skew your budgeting. You can find live pricing data from major retailers or aggregator sites like [https://laravelcompany.com](https://laravelcompany.com) which often track market trends, though for immediate accuracy, checking local station prices is recommended.

The basic formula to determine the cost per mile is:

$$ \text{Cost per Mile} = \frac{\text{Price per Liter}}{\text{Fuel Efficiency (MPG converted)}} $$

Or, working with metric units directly:

$$ \text{Cost per 100km} = \text{L/100km} \times \text{Price per Liter} $$

For example, if your Lexus IS consumes 7.5 liters per 100km and fuel costs Â£1.45 per liter, the cost to drive 100km is Â£10.875. If your Audi TT achieves a slightly higher efficiency of 6.0 L/100km at the same price point, its running cost drops significantly, illustrating how mechanical efficiency directly impacts operational expenditure.

### The Missing Variable: Real-World Variance

The calculation above provides a theoretical maximum range based on ideal conditions. A common pitfall is assuming that the car will consistently hit its official MPG rating. Urban driving with stop-start traffic can reduce fuel economy by 20% to 40%, while highway cruising might push it closer to the official figure. Therefore, when planning long trips, it is safer to derate the calculated range by a margin of 15% to account for these variables.

Additionally, consider the cost of the "reserve" fuel. If you run the car down to the reserve tank before refilling, you are essentially paying for that last bit of fuel at a higher effective rate because you drove fewer miles per liter in that specific segment. For accurate budgeting, treat the full tank calculation as an upper bound and always monitor your range warning light to avoid entering the high-cost reserve zone unless necessary.

By breaking down the problem into capacity verification, efficiency measurement, and dynamic pricing, you can move beyond guesswork and understand exactly how much mileage a full tank will yield in pounds or dollars.
